name: What should be included in a pool renovation quote?

mainEntity.name: What line items should a pool renovation estimate include?
mainEntity.text: What line items should a pool renovation estimate include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A detailed quote is one of the best ways to avoid surprise costs. It should clearly separate demolition, disposal, shell preparation, interior finish, tile, coping, plumbing, electrical, equipment, permits, inspections, startup, and cleanup. If the contractor expects possible hidden issues, the estimate should say how those changes will be handled and priced. Material allowances should be specific enough that you know what is included and what triggers an upgrade charge. Homeowners should also look for exclusions, such as deck repairs, landscaping restoration, or advanced automation, because those items can change the real total significantly. Comparing quotes only by the bottom line can be misleading if one contractor includes far more scope than another. The best estimate is one that makes it easy to see exactly what is being renovated and what is not. That clarity helps protect the budget and makes contractor comparisons much more reliable.
acceptedAnswer.description: A proper pool renovation quote should list demolition, surface prep, materials, labor, tile, coping, plaster or finish type, plumbing changes, equipment upgrades, cleanup, permits, and inspections. It should also explain exclusions, allowances, and any repair contingency for hidden damage.
